guide.title: Documentation guide
guide.description: Read, write, and share documents with diagrams and HTML.
guide.body:
This sample organizes a team's technical documentation into three levels. Expand the sidebar to browse guides, architecture, and reference material.

## Start here

| Goal | Page |
| --- | --- |
| Run the editor | [Getting started](doc:getting-started) |
| Write an article | [Writing guide](doc:writing) |
| Add a diagram | [Figures and HTML](doc:media) |
| Understand the design | [Architecture](doc:architecture) |

## Overview

:::figure(overview.svg)[From source documents to the viewer]

The :::term(docs-root) contains documents, figures, and HTML fragments. The :::term(compiler) validates these files and produces an :::term(artifact).

## Explore resources

Open Resources in the sidebar to inspect figures, document icons, and the intro HTML resource.

:::callout[Try a different language]
- Use the globe icon at the top right of the preview to open another version of this article.
- Untranslated articles display the source until you save a translation.
- The editor language is a separate setting in the gear menu.
:::

getting-started.title: Getting started
getting-started.description: Launch the sample and edit your first document.
getting-started.body:
## Launch the sample

Run this command from the repository root:

```bash
mise run dev
```

Open the URL printed in the terminal. Select an article in the sidebar, edit its title or body, and save your changes.

## Edit a translation

Choose English from the globe icon at the top right of the preview. Changes are saved to the English JSON catalog, while the source Markdown stays unchanged.

To edit another collection:

```bash
mise run edit ../my-docs
```

See [Folder layout](doc:layout) for the shared document hierarchy and resource locations.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.description: How the viewer, compiler, and rendering core work together.
architecture.body:
## Responsibilities

:::term(compiler)
name: "compiler"
definition: "The process that reads source files, validates structure and references, and builds data for viewing and distribution."
:::

:::graph[Component dependencies]
[viewer]: Viewer and editor @app
[compiler]: Compiler @app
[core]: Rendering and types @lib
[viewer] -> [compiler]
[viewer] -> [core]
[compiler] -> [core]
:::

The viewer reads documents and language catalogs. The compiler validates their structure and references. The core renders the result.

See [Processing flow](doc:flow) and [Data model](doc:data-model) for detailed examples.

## Choose a resource

| HTML fragment | Embedded content |

terms.title: Using terms
terms.description: Declare terms in articles and reference them by ID.
terms.body:
Declare a term anywhere in an article body. Declarations are collected automatically into Resources → Terms; no separate registration is needed.

This sample places declarations in [Folder layout](doc:layout), [Architecture](doc:architecture), [Data model](doc:data-model), and [Exporting](doc:publishing).

Use :::term(docs-root) as input to the :::term(compiler), which produces an :::term(artifact).

layout.title: Folder layout
layout.description: Where files live and how to organize the document hierarchy.
layout.body:
## Where source files live

:::term(docs-root)
name: "docs root"
definition: "The input folder containing content/, figures/, and icons/."
description: "Source document collection."
:::

```
sample-content/
  manifest.yaml
  content/
    guide.md
    getting-started.md
    layout.md
  figures/
    overview.svg
    pipeline.html
    intro.html
```

| Location | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `content/<id>.md` | Article body; the filename determines the document ID |
| `manifest.yaml` | Sidebar hierarchy and display order |
| `figures/` | SVG, images, and HTML fragments |

:::term(doc-id)
name: "document ID"
definition: "The Markdown filename without its extension, used by doc: links."
:::

## A three-level hierarchy

:::term(manifest)
name: "manifest"
definition: "The manifest.yaml file defining document hierarchy and order."
:::

Define parent-child relationships in the manifest without dividing files into folders. This page is the third level: Documentation guide → Getting started → Folder layout.

```yaml
title: "Document System"
docs:
  - guide:
      - getting-started:
          - layout
```

`title` is the site title shown in the upper-left corner and browser tab.

Write a document link as `[Getting started](doc:getting-started)`. Renaming the page title preserves links as long as its document ID stays the same.

data-model.title: Data model
data-model.description: A schema example connecting teams, authors, and documents.
data-model.body:
This fictional model demonstrates schema rendering. It is not the database structure used by document-system.

## The writing team model

:::term(schema)
name: "schema"
definition: "The structure of tables, column types, and relationships."
:::

:::schema[Teams and documents]
### Teams
teams:
  id: pk
  name: string

authors:
  id: pk
  team_id: fk(teams)
  name: string

### Content
documents:
  id: pk
  author_id: fk(authors)
  title: string
  status: enum("draft"|"review"|"published")
  updated_at: timestamp

revisions:
  id: pk
  document_id: fk(documents)
  body: string
  created_at: timestamp
:::

## Reading the model

| Relationship | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| teams → authors | Authors belong to teams |
| authors → documents | Authors are responsible for documents |
| documents → revisions | Each document keeps its revision history |

`pk` marks a primary key; `fk(...)` identifies a referenced table. See [Syntax](doc:syntax) for available types.

publishing.title: Exporting
publishing.description: Create JSON, HTML, or ZIP output for your audience.
publishing.body:
## Choose a format

:::term(artifact)
name: "artifact"
definition: "The compiler output: docs.json and a JSON file for each figure."
:::

| Format | Purpose | Default output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JSON | Consume from another application | `dist/artifact/` |
| HTML | Share a single file for reading | `dist/index.html` |
| ZIP | Share editable source files | `dist/<root name>.zip` |

## Export the sample

Run from the repository root:

```bash
mise run export json
mise run export html
mise run export zip
```

Output is saved under `sample-content/dist/`. To use another docs root, pass its path after the format:

```bash
mise run export html ../my-docs
```

:::callout[Before sharing]
- JSON and HTML exports are blocked when validation errors exist.
- Open the generated HTML and check the text and figures. Inspect HTML resources in the editor's resource list.
- Before sharing source files, check that the ZIP contains no unnecessary information.
:::

See the [Publishing checklist](doc:a) for more checks.
